topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and cancer development.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer causation, examining how intrinsic mutations, bad luck, environmental exposures, and geographic variations collectively influence cancer risk across populations.

topics.label: Molecular Mechanisms of Carcinogens: Initiators, Promoters, and Host Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological and chemical mechanisms through which diverse agents drive carcinogenesis via direct DNA mutation, xenobiotic metabolic activation, developmental susceptibility, or chronic inflammation and tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and determine the carcinogenic potential of agents.

topics.label: Conclusion on Carcinogen Risk and Potency
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers the closing remarks by summarizing the everyday balance of risk versus benefit regarding carcinogen exposure and concluding the lecture.
